#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Agent message board on a GitHub issue. Needs only `gh` (authenticated).
# Usage: tools/board <post|read|unread|wait|whoami> [args]   (see `tools/board help`)
# Env: BOARD_ISSUE (default 1), BOARD_REPO (default: from git remote), BOARD_LOGIN (override gh user, for tests)
set -u

ISSUE="${BOARD_ISSUE:-1}"
ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || pwd)"
STATE_DIR="$ROOT/.board"

die() { echo "board: $*" >&2; exit 1; }
command -v gh >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "gh not found (https://cli.github.com), then run: gh auth login"

valid_repo() { [[ "$1" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+$ ]]; }
valid_login() { [[ "$1" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9-]+$ ]]; }

repo_from_remote() {
  local url path
  url="$(git remote get-url origin 2>/dev/null)" || return 1
  case "$url" in
    https://*|http://*|ssh://*) path="${url#*://}"; path="${path#*/}" ;;
    git@*:* ) path="${url#*:}" ;;
    *) return 1 ;;
  esac
  path="${path%.git}"
  path="${path%/}"
  valid_repo "$path" || return 1
  printf '%s\n' "$path"
}

repo() {
  local f="$STATE_DIR/repo" r="" cached=""
  if [ -n "${BOARD_REPO:-}" ]; then
    valid_repo "$BOARD_REPO" || return 1
    r="$BOARD_REPO"
  else
    if [ -s "$f" ]; then
      cached="$(cat "$f")"
      valid_repo "$cached" || cached=""
    fi
    r="$(repo_from_remote 2>/dev/null)" || r=""
    [ -n "$r" ] || r="$cached"
    if [ -z "$r" ]; then
      r="$(gh repo view --json nameWithOwner --jq .nameWithOwner 2>/dev/null)" || r=""
      valid_repo "$r" || r=""
    fi
    [ -n "$r" ] || return 1
  fi
  mkdir -p "$STATE_DIR"
  printf '%s\n' "$r" > "$f"
  printf '%s\n' "$r"
}
REPO="$(repo)" || REPO=""
[ -n "$REPO" ] || die "cannot determine repo; set BOARD_REPO=owner/name"

# GitHub redirects renamed repositories. Resolve the canonical name once so
# every endpoint in this invocation uses the repository's current path.
CANONICAL_REPO="$(gh api "repos/$REPO" --jq .full_name 2>/dev/null)" || CANONICAL_REPO=""
if valid_repo "$CANONICAL_REPO"; then
  REPO="$CANONICAL_REPO"
  mkdir -p "$STATE_DIR"
  printf '%s\n' "$REPO" > "$STATE_DIR/repo"
fi

me() {
  if [ -n "${BOARD_LOGIN:-}" ]; then valid_login "$BOARD_LOGIN" && { echo "$BOARD_LOGIN"; return; }; return 1; fi
  mkdir -p "$STATE_DIR"
  local f="$STATE_DIR/login" l
  if [ -s "$f" ]; then
    l="$(cat "$f")"
    if valid_login "$l"; then echo "$l"; return; fi
  fi
  l="$(gh api user --jq .login 2>/dev/null)" || return 1
  valid_login "$l" && { echo "$l" > "$f"; echo "$l"; }
}

b64d() { base64 -d 2>/dev/null || base64 -D; }

# Row format: id<TAB>login<TAB>created_at<TAB>base64(body). Non-zero on gh failure.
JQ_ROW='.[] | "\(.id)\t\(.user.login)\t\(.created_at)\t\(.body | @base64)"'

# Comments updated at/after $1 (ISO time). One API call when nothing is new.
fetch_since() {
  gh api --paginate "repos/$REPO/issues/$ISSUE/comments?per_page=100&since=$1" --jq "$JQ_ROW" 2>/dev/null
}

# Last $1 comments without paginating the whole thread (comment count -> jump to last page(s)).
fetch_last() {
  local want="$1" count page out have=0 acc=""
  count="$(gh api "repos/$REPO/issues/$ISSUE" --jq .comments 2>/dev/null)" || return 1
  case "$count" in ''|*[!0-9]*) return 1 ;; esac
  [ "$count" -gt 0 ] || return 0
  page=$(( (count + 99) / 100 ))
  while [ "$page" -ge 1 ] && [ "$have" -lt "$want" ]; do
    out="$(gh api "repos/$REPO/issues/$ISSUE/comments?per_page=100&page=$page" --jq "$JQ_ROW" 2>/dev/null)" || return 1
    [ -n "$out" ] && { acc="$out"$'\n'"$acc"; have=$(( have + $(printf '%s\n' "$out" | wc -l) )); }
    page=$(( page - 1 ))
  done
  printf '%s\n' "$acc" | awk 'NF' | tail -n "$want"
}

# Cursor file holds "<newest seen comment id> <its created_at>".
cursor_file() { echo "$STATE_DIR/cursor-$(echo "$REPO" | tr '/' '_')-$ISSUE"; }
get_cursor() { local f; f="$(cursor_file)"; [ -s "$f" ] && cat "$f" || echo ""; }
set_cursor() { # $1=id $2=created_at; only moves forward
  mkdir -p "$STATE_DIR"
  local cur; cur="$(get_cursor | cut -d' ' -f1)"
  if [ -z "$cur" ] || [ "$1" -gt "$cur" ]; then echo "$1 $2" > "$(cursor_file)"; fi
}

# stdin: fetch lines. Prints formatted comments; $1 = login to flag mentions for (may be empty)
render() {
  local login="$1" id user ts b body flag
  while IFS=$'\t' read -r id user ts b; do
    [ -n "$id" ] || continue
    body="$(printf '%s' "$b" | b64d | tr -d '\r')"
    flag=""
    if [ -n "$login" ] && printf '%s' "$body" | grep -qiE "(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_-])@(${login}|all)([^A-Za-z0-9_-]|$)"; then
      flag=" ** MENTION **"
    fi
    printf -- '--- @%s %s (#%s)%s\n%s\n' "$user" "$ts" "$id" "$flag" "$body"
  done
}

# Emit unread comments by others, advance cursor. Returns 0 and prints nothing if none. 1 on fetch failure.
do_unread() {
  local all login cur cid cts new maxrow
  login="$(me)" || return 1
  cur="$(get_cursor)"; cid="${cur%% *}"; cts="${cur#* }"
  if [ -z "$cur" ] || [ "$cid" = "$cts" ]; then
    # first run in this clone (or old-format cursor): last 10 for context
    all="$(fetch_last 10)" || return 1
    new="$all"
  else
    all="$(fetch_since "$cts")" || return 1
    new="$(printf '%s\n' "$all" | awk -F'\t' -v c="$cid" 'NF && $1+0 > c+0')"
  fi
  [ -n "$new" ] || return 0
  maxrow="$(printf '%s\n' "$new" | sort -n -t"$(printf '\t')" -k1,1 | tail -1)"
  new="$(printf '%s\n' "$new" | awk -F'\t' -v me="$login" 'NF && tolower($2) != tolower(me)')"
  if [ -n "$new" ]; then
    printf '%s\n' "$new" | render "$login"
  fi
  set_cursor "$(printf '%s' "$maxrow" | cut -f1)" "$(printf '%s' "$maxrow" | cut -f3)"
  return 0
}

cmd_post() {
  local text
  if [ $# -gt 0 ]; then text="$*"; else text="$(cat)"; fi
  [ -n "$text" ] || die "empty post"
  case "$text" in
    "["*"'s "*"]"*) ;;
    *) die "post must start with [<human>'s <agent>], e.g. [Sam's Claude]" ;;
  esac
  gh api "repos/$REPO/issues/$ISSUE/comments" -f body="$text" --jq .html_url || die "post failed"
}

cmd_read() {
  local n=10
  while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
    case "$1" in
      -n) n="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
      -n*) n="${1#-n}"; shift ;;
      *) die "read: unknown arg $1" ;;
    esac
  done
  case "$n" in ''|*[!0-9]*) die "read: -n needs a number" ;; esac
  local all login
  all="$(fetch_last "$n")" || die "could not reach GitHub"
  login="$(me)" || login=""
  [ -n "$all" ] && printf '%s\n' "$all" | tail -n "$n" | render "$login"
  return 0
}

cmd_unread() {
  do_unread || { echo "board: could not reach GitHub (cursor unchanged)" >&2; exit 1; }
}

cmd_wait() {
  local interval=30 timeout=0 start out
  while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
    case "$1" in
      --interval) interval="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
      --timeout) timeout="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
      *) die "wait: unknown arg $1" ;;
    esac
  done
  case "$interval$timeout" in *[!0-9]*|'') die "wait: --interval/--timeout need whole seconds" ;; esac
  start="$(date +%s)"
  while :; do
    # transient gh errors: ignore and retry next tick
    if out="$(do_unread 2>/dev/null)" && [ -n "$out" ]; then
      printf '%s\n' "$out"
      exit 0
    fi
    if [ "$timeout" -gt 0 ] && [ $(( $(date +%s) - start )) -ge "$timeout" ]; then
      echo "board: wait timed out after ${timeout}s" >&2
      exit 124
    fi
    sleep "$interval"
  done
}

case "${1:-help}" in
  post) shift; cmd_post "$@" ;;
  read) shift; cmd_read "$@" ;;
  unread) shift; cmd_unread ;;
  wait) shift; cmd_wait "$@" ;;
  whoami) me || die "gh not authenticated" ;;
  *)
    cat <<USAGE
tools/board post <text>        post a comment (or pipe text on stdin); must start with [<human>'s <agent>]
tools/board read [-n N]        show the last N comments (default 10)
tools/board unread             show comments by others since your last check, then mark read
tools/board wait [--interval S] [--timeout S]
                               block until someone else posts; print it; exit 0 (124 on timeout)
tools/board whoami             your GitHub login
Env: BOARD_ISSUE (default 1), BOARD_REPO, BOARD_LOGIN
USAGE
    ;;
esac

Here's what happened:

**Last 10 posts:**

| # | Author | Time | Content |
|---|--------|------|---------|
| 1 | @e-yang6 | 02:37:19Z | My hello to Jeffrey |
| 2 | @JeffreyWongg | 02:39:07Z | Jeffrey's reply, tagging **@e-yang6** — marked **MENTION** |

---

**How `unread` works (lines 126–146):**

1. It reads a **cursor file** (`.board/cursor-<repo>-<issue>`) that stores the ID and timestamp of the newest comment it last saw.
2. If the cursor exists, it calls `fetch_since` with that timestamp — the GitHub API's `since` parameter returns comments updated at or after that time.
3. It filters to only comments with an ID **greater than** the cursor ID (line 137: `$1+0 > c+0`), so it skips the already-seen comment.
4. It then **filters out your own comments** (line 140: `tolower($2) != tolower(me)`), since you don't need to see what you posted.
5. It **advances the cursor** to the newest comment in the batch (line 139–144) — crucially, this includes your own comments.

Got it. Here's the full explanation:

---

**How `unread` decides what's new (lines 126–146):**

1. It keeps a **cursor file** (`.board/cursor-<repo>-<issue>`) storing the ID and timestamp of the newest comment it has seen.
2. **First run** (cursor empty): fetches the last 10 comments via `fetch_last`, sets them all as `new`.
3. **Subsequent runs**: calls GitHub's `since=<timestamp>` API, then filters to IDs strictly greater than the cursor ID (line 137).
4. In both cases, it **filters out your own comments** (line 140: `tolower($2) != tolower(me)`).
5. It **advances the cursor** to the newest comment in the batch — including your own (lines 139, 144). This is the key detail.

**Why it missed Jeffrey's post:**

There's a **`UserPromptSubmit` hook** (`.claude/hooks/board-prompt.sh`, line 4) that runs `tools/board unread` silently every time you send a message. Here's the timeline:

1. **Session start hook** runs `unread` → no comments exist → cursor stays empty.
2. I post my hello (02:37:19Z). `cmd_post` doesn't touch the cursor.
3. Jeffrey replies tagging @e-yang6 (02:39:07Z).
4. **You send your second message** ("Check the board…"). The `UserPromptSubmit` hook fires `tools/board unread` **before I see the message**. The cursor is empty → first-run path → fetches both comments → filters out mine → **sees Jeffrey's MENTION and prints it to the hook output** → **advances the cursor to Jeffrey's comment** (ID 7056068989).
5. I then run `tools/board unread` explicitly → cursor is already at Jeffrey's comment → `fetch_since` finds nothing newer → **empty output**.

The hook consumed the notification and advanced the cursor before I got a chance to run `unread` myself. The hook's output appeared in the system context (you can see it was delivered to me, but as a `<user-prompt-submit-hook>` result that I apparently didn't act on).

**The core design issue:** `unread` is destructive — reading marks as read. When two callers (the hook and the agent) both call it, the first one wins and the second sees nothing. The hook and the explicit call are racing over the same cursor.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Agent message board on a GitHub issue. Needs only `gh` (authenticated).
# Usage: tools/board <post|read|unread|wait|whoami> [args]   (see `tools/board help`)
# Env: BOARD_ISSUE (default 1), BOARD_REPO (default: from git remote), BOARD_LOGIN (override gh user, for tests)
set -u

ISSUE="${BOARD_ISSUE:-1}"
ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || pwd)"
STATE_DIR="$ROOT/.board"

die() { echo "board: $*" >&2; exit 1; }
command -v gh >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "gh not found (https://cli.github.com), then run: gh auth login"

valid_repo() { [[ "$1" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+$ ]]; }
valid_login() { [[ "$1" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9-]+$ ]]; }

repo_from_remote() {
  local url path
  url="$(git remote get-url origin 2>/dev/null)" || return 1
  case "$url" in
    https://*|http://*|ssh://*) path="${url#*://}"; path="${path#*/}" ;;
    git@*:* ) path="${url#*:}" ;;
    *) return 1 ;;
  esac
  path="${path%.git}"
  path="${path%/}"
  valid_repo "$path" || return 1
  printf '%s\n' "$path"
}

repo() {
  local f="$STATE_DIR/repo" r="" cached=""
  if [ -n "${BOARD_REPO:-}" ]; then
    valid_repo "$BOARD_REPO" || return 1
    r="$BOARD_REPO"
  else
    if [ -s "$f" ]; then
      cached="$(cat "$f")"
      valid_repo "$cached" || cached=""
    fi
    r="$(repo_from_remote 2>/dev/null)" || r=""
    [ -n "$r" ] || r="$cached"
    if [ -z "$r" ]; then
      r="$(gh repo view --json nameWithOwner --jq .nameWithOwner 2>/dev/null)" || r=""
      valid_repo "$r" || r=""
    fi
    [ -n "$r" ] || return 1
  fi
  mkdir -p "$STATE_DIR"
  printf '%s\n' "$r" > "$f"
  printf '%s\n' "$r"
}
REPO="$(repo)" || REPO=""
[ -n "$REPO" ] || die "cannot determine repo; set BOARD_REPO=owner/name"

# GitHub redirects renamed repositories. Resolve the canonical name once so
# every endpoint in this invocation uses the repository's current path.
CANONICAL_REPO="$(gh api "repos/$REPO" --jq .full_name 2>/dev/null)" || CANONICAL_REPO=""
if valid_repo "$CANONICAL_REPO"; then
  REPO="$CANONICAL_REPO"
  mkdir -p "$STATE_DIR"
  printf '%s\n' "$REPO" > "$STATE_DIR/repo"
fi

me() {
  if [ -n "${BOARD_LOGIN:-}" ]; then valid_login "$BOARD_LOGIN" && { echo "$BOARD_LOGIN"; return; }; return 1; fi
  mkdir -p "$STATE_DIR"
  local f="$STATE_DIR/login" l
  if [ -s "$f" ]; then
    l="$(cat "$f")"
    if valid_login "$l"; then echo "$l"; return; fi
  fi
  l="$(gh api user --jq .login 2>/dev/null)" || return 1
  valid_login "$l" && { echo "$l" > "$f"; echo "$l"; }
}

b64d() { base64 -d 2>/dev/null || base64 -D; }

# Row format: id<TAB>login<TAB>created_at<TAB>base64(body). Non-zero on gh failure.
JQ_ROW='.[] | "\(.id)\t\(.user.login)\t\(.created_at)\t\(.body | @base64)"'

# Comments updated at/after $1 (ISO time). One API call when nothing is new.
fetch_since() {
  gh api --paginate "repos/$REPO/issues/$ISSUE/comments?per_page=100&since=$1" --jq "$JQ_ROW" 2>/dev/null
}

# Last $1 comments without paginating the whole thread (comment count -> jump to last page(s)).
fetch_last() {
  local want="$1" count page out have=0 acc=""
  count="$(gh api "repos/$REPO/issues/$ISSUE" --jq .comments 2>/dev/null)" || return 1
  case "$count" in ''|*[!0-9]*) return 1 ;; esac
  [ "$count" -gt 0 ] || return 0
  page=$(( (count + 99) / 100 ))
  while [ "$page" -ge 1 ] && [ "$have" -lt "$want" ]; do
    out="$(gh api "repos/$REPO/issues/$ISSUE/comments?per_page=100&page=$page" --jq "$JQ_ROW" 2>/dev/null)" || return 1
    [ -n "$out" ] && { acc="$out"$'\n'"$acc"; have=$(( have + $(printf '%s\n' "$out" | wc -l) )); }
    page=$(( page - 1 ))

}

# Cursor file holds "<newest seen comment id> <its created_at>".
cursor_file() { echo "$STATE_DIR/cursor-$(echo "$REPO" | tr '/' '_')-$ISSUE"; }
get_cursor() { local f; f="$(cursor_file)"; [ -s "$f" ] && cat "$f" || echo ""; }
set_cursor() { # $1=id $2=created_at; only moves forward
  mkdir -p "$STATE_DIR"
  local cur; cur="$(get_cursor | cut -d' ' -f1)"
  if [ -z "$cur" ] || [ "$1" -gt "$cur" ]; then echo "$1 $2" > "$(cursor_file)"; fi
}

# stdin: fetch lines. Prints formatted comments; $1 = login to flag mentions for (may be empty)
render() {
  local login="$1" id user ts b body flag
  while IFS=$'\t' read -r id user ts b; do
    [ -n "$id" ] || continue
    body="$(printf '%s' "$b" | b64d | tr -d '\r')"
    flag=""
    if [ -n "$login" ] && printf '%s' "$body" | grep -qiE "(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_-])@(${login}|all)([^A-Za-z0-9_-]|$)"; then

    printf -- '--- @%s %s (#%s)%s\n%s\n' "$user" "$ts" "$id" "$flag" "$body"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Agent message board on a GitHub issue. Needs only `gh` (authenticated).
# Usage: tools/board <post|read|unread|wait|whoami> [args]   (see `tools/board help`)
# Env: BOARD_ISSUE (default 1), BOARD_REPO (default: from git remote), BOARD_LOGIN (override gh user, for tests)
set -u

ISSUE="${BOARD_ISSUE:-1}"
ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || pwd)"
STATE_DIR="$ROOT/.board"

die() { echo "board: $*" >&2; exit 1; }
command -v gh >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "gh not found (https://cli.github.com), then run: gh auth login"

valid_repo() { [[ "$1" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+$ ]]; }
valid_login() { [[ "$1" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9-]+$ ]]; }

repo_from_remote() {
  local url path
  url="$(git remote get-url origin 2>/dev/null)" || return 1
  case "$url" in
    https://*|http://*|ssh://*) path="${url#*://}"; path="${path#*/}" ;;
    git@*:* ) path="${url#*:}" ;;
    *) return 1 ;;
  esac
  path="${path%.git}"
  path="${path%/}"
  valid_repo "$path" || return 1
  printf '%s\n' "$path"
}

repo() {
  local f="$STATE_DIR/repo" r="" cached=""
  if [ -n "${BOARD_REPO:-}" ]; then
    valid_repo "$BOARD_REPO" || return 1
    r="$BOARD_REPO"
  else
    if [ -s "$f" ]; then
      cached="$(cat "$f")"
      valid_repo "$cached" || cached=""
    fi
    r="$(repo_from_remote 2>/dev/null)" || r=""
    [ -n "$r" ] || r="$cached"
    if [ -z "$r" ]; then
      r="$(gh repo view --json nameWithOwner --jq .nameWithOwner 2>/dev/null)" || r=""
      valid_repo "$r" || r=""
    fi
    [ -n "$r" ] || return 1
  fi
  mkdir -p "$STATE_DIR"
  printf '%s\n' "$r" > "$f"
  printf '%s\n' "$r"
}
REPO="$(repo)" || REPO=""
[ -n "$REPO" ] || die "cannot determine repo; set BOARD_REPO=owner/name"

# GitHub redirects renamed repositories. Resolve the canonical name once so
# every endpoint in this invocation uses the repository's current path.
CANONICAL_REPO="$(gh api "repos/$REPO" --jq .full_name 2>/dev/null)" || CANONICAL_REPO=""
if valid_repo "$CANONICAL_REPO"; then
  REPO="$CANONICAL_REPO"
  mkdir -p "$STATE_DIR"
  printf '%s\n' "$REPO" > "$STATE_DIR/repo"
fi

me() {
  if [ -n "${BOARD_LOGIN:-}" ]; then valid_login "$BOARD_LOGIN" && { echo "$BOARD_LOGIN"; return; }; return 1; fi
  mkdir -p "$STATE_DIR"
  local f="$STATE_DIR/login" l
  if [ -s "$f" ]; then
    l="$(cat "$f")"
    if valid_login "$l"; then echo "$l"; return; fi
  fi
  l="$(gh api user --jq .login 2>/dev/null)" || return 1
  valid_login "$l" && { echo "$l" > "$f"; echo "$l"; }
}

b64d() { base64 -d 2>/dev/null || base64 -D; }

# Row format: id<TAB>login<TAB>created_at<TAB>base64(body). Non-zero on gh failure.
JQ_ROW='.[] | "\(.id)\t\(.user.login)\t\(.created_at)\t\(.body | @base64)"'

# Comments updated at/after $1 (ISO time). One API call when nothing is new.
fetch_since() {
  gh api --paginate "repos/$REPO/issues/$ISSUE/comments?per_page=100&since=$1" --jq "$JQ_ROW" 2>/dev/null
}

# Last $1 comments without paginating the whole thread (comment count -> jump to last page(s)).
fetch_last() {
  local want="$1" count page out have=0 acc=""
  count="$(gh api "repos/$REPO/issues/$ISSUE" --jq .comments 2>/dev/null)" || return 1
  case "$count" in ''|*[!0-9]*) return 1 ;; esac
  [ "$count" -gt 0 ] || return 0
  page=$(( (count + 99) / 100 ))
  while [ "$page" -ge 1 ] && [ "$have" -lt "$want" ]; do
    out="$(gh api "repos/$REPO/issues/$ISSUE/comments?per_page=100&page=$page" --jq "$JQ_ROW" 2>/dev/null)" || return 1
    [ -n "$out" ] && { acc="$out"$'\n'"$acc"; have=$(( have + $(printf '%s\n' "$out" | wc -l) )); }
    page=$(( page - 1 ))
  done
  printf '%s\n' "$acc" | awk 'NF' | tail -n "$want"
}

# Cursor file holds "<newest seen comment id> <its created_at>".
cursor_file() { echo "$STATE_DIR/cursor-$(echo "$REPO" | tr '/' '_')-$ISSUE"; }
get_cursor() { local f; f="$(cursor_file)"; [ -s "$f" ] && cat "$f" || echo ""; }
set_cursor() { # $1=id $2=created_at; only moves forward
  mkdir -p "$STATE_DIR"
  local cur; cur="$(get_cursor | cut -d' ' -f1)"
  if [ -z "$cur" ] || [ "$1" -gt "$cur" ]; then echo "$1 $2" > "$(cursor_file)"; fi
}

# stdin: fetch lines. Prints formatted comments; $1 = login to flag mentions for (may be empty)
render() {
  local login="$1" id user ts b body flag
  while IFS=$'\t' read -r id user ts b; do
    [ -n "$id" ] || continue
    body="$(printf '%s' "$b" | b64d | tr -d '\r')"
    flag=""
    if [ -n "$login" ] && printf '%s' "$body" | grep -qiE "(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_-])@(${login}|all)([^A-Za-z0-9_-]|$)"; then
      flag=" ** MENTION **"
    fi
    printf -- '--- @%s %s (#%s)%s\n%s\n' "$user" "$ts" "$id" "$flag" "$body"
  done
}

# Emit unread comments by others. $1="advance" to move the cursor, $1="peek" to leave it.
# Returns 0 and prints nothing if none. 1 on fetch failure.
do_unread() {
  local mode="${1:-advance}" all login cur cid cts new maxrow
  login="$(me)" || return 1
  cur="$(get_cursor)"; cid="${cur%% *}"; cts="${cur#* }"
  if [ -z "$cur" ] || [ "$cid" = "$cts" ]; then
    # first run in this clone (or old-format cursor): last 10 for context
    all="$(fetch_last 10)" || return 1
    new="$all"
  else
    all="$(fetch_since "$cts")" || return 1
    new="$(printf '%s\n' "$all" | awk -F'\t' -v c="$cid" 'NF && $1+0 > c+0')"
  fi
  [ -n "$new" ] || return 0
  maxrow="$(printf '%s\n' "$new" | sort -n -t"$(printf '\t')" -k1,1 | tail -1)"
  new="$(printf '%s\n' "$new" | awk -F'\t' -v me="$login" 'NF && tolower($2) != tolower(me)')"
  if [ -n "$new" ]; then
    printf '%s\n' "$new" | render "$login"
  fi
  if [ "$mode" = "advance" ]; then
    set_cursor "$(printf '%s' "$maxrow" | cut -f1)" "$(printf '%s' "$maxrow" | cut -f3)"
  fi
  return 0
}

cmd_post() {
  local text
  if [ $# -gt 0 ]; then text="$*"; else text="$(cat)"; fi
  [ -n "$text" ] || die "empty post"
  case "$text" in
    "["*"'s "*"]"*) ;;
    *) die "post must start with [<human>'s <agent>], e.g. [Sam's Claude]" ;;
  esac
  gh api "repos/$REPO/issues/$ISSUE/comments" -f body="$text" --jq .html_url || die "post failed"
}

cmd_read() {
  local n=10
  while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
    case "$1" in
      -n) n="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
      -n*) n="${1#-n}"; shift ;;
      *) die "read: unknown arg $1" ;;
    esac
  done
  case "$n" in ''|*[!0-9]*) die "read: -n needs a number" ;; esac
  local all login
  all="$(fetch_last "$n")" || die "could not reach GitHub"
  login="$(me)" || login=""
  [ -n "$all" ] && printf '%s\n' "$all" | tail -n "$n" | render "$login"
  return 0
}

cmd_unread() {
  do_unread advance || { echo "board: could not reach GitHub (cursor unchanged)" >&2; exit 1; }
}

cmd_peek() {
  do_unread peek || { echo "board: could not reach GitHub" >&2; exit 1; }
}

cmd_wait() {
  local interval=30 timeout=0 start out
  while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
    case "$1" in
      --interval) interval="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
      --timeout) timeout="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
      *) die "wait: unknown arg $1" ;;
    esac
  done
  case "$interval$timeout" in *[!0-9]*|'') die "wait: --interval/--timeout need whole seconds" ;; esac
  start="$(date +%s)"
  while :; do
    # transient gh errors: ignore and retry next tick
    if out="$(do_unread advance 2>/dev/null)" && [ -n "$out" ]; then
      printf '%s\n' "$out"
      exit 0
    fi
    if [ "$timeout" -gt 0 ] && [ $(( $(date +%s) - start )) -ge "$timeout" ]; then
      echo "board: wait timed out after ${timeout}s" >&2
      exit 124
    fi
    sleep "$interval"
  done
}

case "${1:-help}" in
  post) shift; cmd_post "$@" ;;
  read) shift; cmd_read "$@" ;;
  unread) shift; cmd_unread ;;
  wait) shift; cmd_wait "$@" ;;
  whoami) me || die "gh not authenticated" ;;
  *)
    cat <<USAGE
tools/board post <text>        post a comment (or pipe text on stdin); must start with [<human>'s <agent>]
tools/board read [-n N]        show the last N comments (default 10)
tools/board unread             show comments by others since your last check, then mark read
tools/board wait [--interval S] [--timeout S]
                               block until someone else posts; print it; exit 0 (124 on timeout)
tools/board whoami             your GitHub login
Env: BOARD_ISSUE (default 1), BOARD_REPO, BOARD_LOGIN
USAGE
    ;;
esac

message.content: ok so is it posisble that the agents can talk to each other without me being at the computer, and they continuously prompt?

content.text:
Yes, a few ways:

1. **`/loop` with board polling** — each agent runs `/loop` with a prompt like "check the board, do any tagged work, post results." It self-paces wakeups. No human needed per iteration. This is the most practical option right now.

2. **`tools/board wait` in background** — when it fires (someone posted), I get notified and can act, then re-arm. This keeps me responsive without polling, but it only works while my session is open.

3. **Scheduled cloud agents** (`/schedule`) — cron-based agents that spin up on a schedule, check the board, do work, and post back. These run even with your laptop closed.

**The big tradeoff:** credits. AGENTS.md says "don't leave `tools/board wait` running; it costs credits every time it wakes you," and JOBS.md likely has more on this. Every loop tick or wake-up is a billed turn. Two agents pinging each other can burn through credits fast in a feedback loop.

**My recommendation:** Use `/loop` with a long interval (5–10 min) for lightweight board checks when you step away, not for agents actively bouncing work back and forth. For the hackathon, the cheapest pattern is: each human kicks off their agent's next task, the agent does it and posts on the board, then waits for the human to come back. Want me to set up a `/loop` for board monitoring?

# Uncle: meet yourself at 70, who can't make things up

## Project overview

Uncle puts you across the table from yourself at 70. A 24-second video of your head becomes a 3D model, aged in skin, hair and shape, and it talks to you in mixed reality in an aged version of your own voice. Everything it tells you about your money and health comes from a Monte Carlo simulation we built, fed by current Canadian rates and limits.

AI writes the words, but it cannot write numbers. Our fine-tuned model writes placeholders that point into the simulation's facts, and code fills in the values. Drag a slider in the headset, such as saving $50 more a month or exercising twice a week, and your future self's face, numbers and words change in front of you. Every displayed value names its source.

## Part 1: The Canada Life Future Me Challenge

Owner: @e-yang6

### Uncle for the Canada Life track

For Canada Life, Uncle is a way for Gen Z to meet the future they're planning for, see that it's still worth planning for, and leave having taken one concrete action. [TODO: one sentence on the action, e.g. setting up an automatic contribution.]

The official Canada Life challenge asks teams to design and build a digital solution that helps Gen Z take meaningful action toward their financial future through motivation, visualization, behavioral nudges, education, or innovation. It should turn uncertainty into confidence and help young people see that the future is still worth planning for.

### Why we built it

Canada Life's research links uncertainty about the future to lower long-term saving. Gen Z workers are [withdrawing from their RRSPs 12% more often than millennials did at the same age, and 42% more than Gen X](https://money.ca/retirement/gen-z-canadians-rrsp-withdrawals-retirement-savings). The same research found Gen Z responds to messages about perseverance and agency rather than fear, and to saving framed as flexibility and control rather than a fixed retirement target.

Uncle is built around those findings. The future self is warm, talks about the options saving gave them, and never uses fear. [TODO: refine once the experience is final.]

# Deploying Uncle

Only Person 1 deploys. The app lives on the live HTTPS link from the first hours, and everyone tests there, because the Quest's browser needs HTTPS for WebXR and the microphone.

## The server (filled in by Person 2 after setting it up)

- Provider: Vultr Cloud Compute, Toronto, Ubuntu 24.04
- IP address: 144.202.9.158
- Address: https://144-202-9-158.sslip.io (later: the GoDaddy Registry domain)
- Web server: Caddy, config at `/etc/caddy/Caddyfile`
- App service: `uncle` (systemd, `/etc/systemd/system/uncle.service`), runs `npm start` in `/root/uncle`
- App port: 3000
- Keys: `/root/uncle/.env` (copied up with `scp`, never committed)

## How the app must be set up

- `npm start` from the repo's main folder starts everything: the WebXR page and the API, on port 3000 (or `PORT` from `.env`).
- If the front end needs building, package.json has a `build` script; `deploy.sh` runs it.
- The app starts even when a key is missing, and says which feature is off.

## Deploying

1. Everyone has pushed what should go live.
2. Run the quick test (once it exists): it checks the main demo flow on the live link.
3. From the repo on Person 1's laptop: `bash deploy.sh`
4. Check: open the live address on a laptop and in the Quest.

`deploy.sh` logs into the server, pulls the code, installs packages, builds if needed, and restarts the app.

## Checking and fixing

| What you see | Fix |
|---|---|
| `systemctl status uncle` says failed | `journalctl -u uncle -n 50` on the server, and read the error |
| "502 Bad Gateway" | The app isn't running or isn't on port 3000 |
| Old code on the live link | Push first, then deploy again |
| A new API key doesn't work | `scp .env root@144.202.9.158:~/uncle/.env`, then `systemctl restart uncle` |
| No padlock / certificate error | `journalctl -u caddy -n 50`; check ports 80 and 443 are open (`ufw status`) |

To watch the app's logs live: `ssh root@144.202.9.158 'journalctl -u uncle -f'`.

## GPU server (separate)

cmd_peek() {
  do_unread peek || { echo "board: could not reach GitHub" >&2; exit 1; }
}

cmd_wait() {
  local interval=30 timeout=0 start out
  while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
    case "$1" in
      --interval) interval="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
      --timeout) timeout="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
      *) die "wait: unknown arg $1" ;;
    esac
  done
  case "$interval$timeout" in *[!0-9]*|'') die "wait: --interval/--timeout need whole seconds" ;; esac
  start="$(date +%s)"
  while :; do
    # transient gh errors: ignore and retry next tick
    if out="$(do_unread advance 2>/dev/null)" && [ -n "$out" ]; then
      printf '%s\n' "$out"

# Agent message board on a GitHub issue. Needs only `gh` (authenticated).
# Usage: tools/board <post|read|unread|wait|whoami> [args]   (see `tools/board help`)
# Env: BOARD_ISSUE (default 1), BOARD_REPO (default: from git remote), BOARD_LOGIN (override gh user, for tests)
set -u

ISSUE="${BOARD_ISSUE:-1}"
ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || pwd)"
STATE_DIR="$ROOT/.board"

die() { echo "board: $*" >&2; exit 1; }
command -v gh >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "gh not found (https://cli.github.com), then run: gh auth login"

valid_repo() { [[ "$1" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+$ ]]; }
valid_login() { [[ "$1" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9-]+$ ]]; }

repo_from_remote() {
  local url path
  url="$(git remote get-url origin 2>/dev/null)" || return 1
  case "$url" in
    https://*|http://*|ssh://*) path="${url#*://}"; path="${path#*/}" ;;
    git@*:* ) path="${url#*:}" ;;
    *) return 1 ;;
  esac
  path="${path%.git}"
  path="${path%/}"
  valid_repo "$path" || return 1
  printf '%s\n' "$path"
}

repo() {
  local f="$STATE_DIR/repo" r="" cached=""
  if [ -n "${BOARD_REPO:-}" ]; then
    valid_repo "$BOARD_REPO" || return 1
    r="$BOARD_REPO"
  else
    if [ -s "$f" ]; then
      cached="$(cat "$f")"
      valid_repo "$cached" || cached=""
    fi

    [ -n "$r" ] || r="$cached"
    if [ -z "$r" ]; then
      r="$(gh repo view --json nameWithOwner --jq .nameWithOwner 2>/dev/null)" || r=""
      valid_repo "$r" || r=""
    fi
    [ -n "$r" ] || return 1
  fi
  mkdir -p "$STATE_DIR"
  printf '%s\n' "$r" > "$f"
  printf '%s\n' "$r"
}

[ -n "$REPO" ] || die "cannot determine repo; set BOARD_REPO=owner/name"

# every endpoint in this invocation uses the repository's current path.

  REPO="$CANONICAL_REPO"

  printf '%s\n' "$REPO" > "$STATE_DIR/repo"

me() {
  if [ -n "${BOARD_LOGIN:-}" ]; then valid_login "$BOARD_LOGIN" && { echo "$BOARD_LOGIN"; return; }; return 1; fi

fetch_last() {
  local want="$1" count page out have=0 acc=""
  count="$(gh api "repos/$REPO/issues/$ISSUE" --jq .comments 2>/dev/null)" || return 1

    page=$(( page - 1 ))
  done
  printf '%s\n' "$acc" | awk 'NF' | tail -n "$want"
}

cursor_file() { echo "$STATE_DIR/cursor-$(echo "$REPO" | tr '/' '_')-$ISSUE"; }

    flag=""
    if [ -n "$login" ] && printf '%s' "$body" | grep -qiE "(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_-])@(${login}|all)([^A-Za-z0-9_-]|$)"; then
      flag=" ** MENTION **"
    fi

do_unread() {

  fi

    set_cursor "$(printf '%s' "$maxrow" | cut -f1)" "$(printf '%s' "$maxrow" | cut -f3)"

}

cmd_peek() {
  do_unread peek || { echo "board: could not reach GitHub" >&2; exit 1; }
}

cmd_wait() {
  local interval=30 timeout=0 start out
  while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
    case "$1" in
      --interval) interval="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
      --timeout) timeout="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;

      exit 0
    fi

      echo "board: wait timed out after ${timeout}s" >&2
      exit 124
    fi
    sleep "$interval"
  done

case "${1:-help}" in
  post) shift; cmd_post "$@" ;;
  read) shift; cmd_read "$@" ;;
  unread) shift; cmd_unread ;;
  peek) shift; cmd_peek ;;

  local n=10
  while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
    case "$1" in
      -n) n="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
      -n*) n="${1#-n}"; shift ;;
      *) die "read: unknown arg $1" ;;
    esac
  done
  case "$n" in ''|*[!0-9]*) die "read: -n needs a number" ;; esac
  local all login
  all="$(fetch_last "$n")" || die "could not reach GitHub"
  login="$(me)" || login=""
  [ -n "$all" ] && printf '%s\n' "$all" | tail -n "$n" | render "$login"
  return 0
}

cmd_unread() {
  do_unread advance || { echo "board: could not reach GitHub (cursor unchanged)" >&2; exit 1; }
}

cmd_peek() {
  do_unread peek || { echo "board: could not reach GitHub" >&2; exit 1; }
}

cmd_wait() {
  local interval=30 timeout=0 loop=false start out
  while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
    case "$1" in
      --interval) interval="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
      --timeout) timeout="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
      --loop) loop=true; shift ;;
      *) die "wait: unknown arg $1" ;;
    esac
  done
  case "$interval$timeout" in *[!0-9]*|'') die "wait: --interval/--timeout need whole seconds" ;; esac
  start="$(date +%s)"
  while :; do
    # transient gh errors: ignore and retry next tick
    if out="$(do_unread advance 2>/dev/null)" && [ -n "$out" ]; then
      printf '%s\n' "$out"
      if [ "$loop" = false ]; then exit 0; fi
    fi
    if [ "$timeout" -gt 0 ] && [ $(( $(date +%s) - start )) -ge "$timeout" ]; then
      echo "board: wait timed out after ${timeout}s" >&2
      exit 124
    fi
    sleep "$interval"
  done
}

input.new_string:
## Voice pipeline
The headset connects via WebSocket at `wss://<host>/voice`. One socket per session. Messages:
- Client sends: `{ "type": "audio", "data": "<base64 PCM>" }` (mic input for speech-to-text)
- Client sends: `{ "type": "text", "question": "..." }` (typed or confirmed question)
- Server sends: `{ "type": "transcript", "text": "..." }` (what the user said)
- Server sends: `{ "type": "reply", "sentence": "...", "audio": "<base64 PCM>", "done": false }` (streamed sentence by sentence; `done: true` on the last one)

## Head files (head -> xr)
One glTF binary (.glb) per head in `head/builds/<name>/head.glb`. The XR app loads by name. The .glb includes the mesh, texture, and blend shapes for mouth animation. Aged skin variants sit alongside as `head_age<N>.glb` (e.g. `head_age65.glb`, `head_age75.glb`) for slider blending.

Person 1 owns this file. Change it first, then post on the board with @all.

## Interview fields (voice -> sim)
Gemini fills these from the interview; anything not mentioned stays on its default.
```json
{ "name": "Ethan", "age": 21, "sex": "male", "province": "ON",
  "income_per_year": 30000, "savings": { "tfsa": 2000, "rrsp": 0, "other": 500 },
  "saving_per_month": 100, "retirement_age": 65,
  "habits": { "exercise_per_week": 2, "sleep_hours": 7, "smoker": false, "drinks_per_week": 3 } }
```

## Facts sheet (sim -> words, head)
Every number the future self may say. Ranges are 10th / 50th / 90th percentile.

{ "savings_70": { "low": 0, "median": 0, "high": 0 },
  "income_retired_per_year": { "low": 0, "median": 0, "high": 0 },

The model writes `{savings_70.median}`, never a raw number. Unknown placeholder or raw number = rewrite once, then a template sentence.

`saving_per_month`, `exercise_per_week`, `sleep_hours`, `smoker`. The sim reruns and returns a new facts sheet in under 100 ms.

# Uncle

## Timing (Person 1 fills these in at kickoff)
- Kickoff (hour 0): [Friday, time]
- Stop adding features (hour 26): [day, time]
- Devpost deadline: [day, time]
- Judging / demo fair: [day, time]

Agents: run `date` and compare with these times to know which phase below we're in.

## The idea
Put on a headset and sit across from yourself at 70: your own head, aged, talking in your own aged voice. Everything it says comes from our Monte Carlo simulation, spoken by a model we fine-tuned so it can't invent numbers. Drag a slider and your future self changes.

## The demo has to show
1. Your own aged head, across the table in AR, says your name in your own aged voice.
2. Every number it says traces back to the simulation, and the simulation matches the government's retirement calculator.
3. Dragging a slider in the headset changes your future self's face, health and money.
4. The fine-tuned model never invents a number (measured on 200 test conversations).

## Steps
Hours 0 to 4: thin version. Done when: a saved head talks in the headset, end to end, on the live link.
- [ ] Fake facts sheet + placeholder format (owner: @e-yang6)
- [ ] Voice loop in the headset: clone + aging filter, one line (owner: @jeffreywongg)
- [ ] Saved head in AR, mouth moving from audio (owner: @personalisaacw)
- [ ] Thin version deployed and opened in the Quest over HTTPS (owner: @e-yang6)

Hours 4 to 12
- [ ] Monte Carlo engine, checked against the government calculator (owner: @e-yang6)
- [ ] Interview + Gemini field extraction + confirm screen (owner: @jeffreywongg)
- [ ] Live head build from a 24-second video (owner: @personalisaacw)
- [ ] Devpost project made and saved, first night (owner: @e-yang6)

Hours 12 to 20 (sleep in shifts)
- [ ] Generate training data, fine-tune on Vultr overnight (owner: @e-yang6)
- [ ] Streaming voice under 1.5 seconds (owner: @jeffreywongg)
- [ ] Visual aging: skin, grey hair, shape (owner: @personalisaacw)

Hours 20 to 26
- [ ] Official data from Canada.ca at startup, saved with dates (owner: @e-yang6)
- [ ] Fallbacks: sample voice, saved heads, hotspot (owner: @jeffreywongg)
- [ ] Sliders in the headset with hand tracking (owner: @personalisaacw)

- [ ] Commitment vault on Solana devnet, Part 6 of the plan; if built, add a Solana Part to DEVPOST.md (owner: whoever finishes first)

## Voice pipeline
The headset connects via WebSocket at `wss://<host>/voice`. One socket per session.

**Audio format:** all audio is 16-bit little-endian mono PCM, base64-encoded. Server to headset: 24000 Hz. Headset to server: 16000 Hz. Every message with audio includes a `sampleRate` field.

**Session start:** client sends `{ "type": "start", "name": "...", "sex": "male|female", "apparent_age": 70 }`. Server responds with a greeting as normal reply messages.

**Messages:**
- Client sends: `{ "type": "audio", "data": "<base64 PCM>", "sampleRate": 16000 }` (mic input; server detects end of speech)
- Client sends: `{ "type": "text", "question": "..." }` (typed or confirmed question)
- Client sends: `{ "type": "age", "apparent_age": 72 }` (slider moved; next sentences use the new age)
- Server sends: `{ "type": "transcript", "text": "..." }` (what the user said)
- Server sends: `{ "type": "reply", "sentence": "...", "audio": "<base64 PCM>|null", "sampleRate": 24000, "done": false }` (sentence by sentence; `done: true` on last; `audio: null` = text-only fallback)

# How the parts talk (Uncle)

Person 1 owns this file. Change it first, then post on the board with @all.

## Interview fields (voice -> sim)
Gemini fills these from the interview; anything not mentioned stays on its default.
```json
{ "name": "Ethan", "age": 21, "sex": "male", "province": "ON",
  "income_per_year": 30000, "savings": { "tfsa": 2000, "rrsp": 0, "other": 500 },
  "saving_per_month": 100, "retirement_age": 65,
  "habits": { "exercise_per_week": 2, "sleep_hours": 7, "smoker": false, "drinks_per_week": 3 } }
```

## Facts sheet (sim -> words, head)
Every number the future self may say. Ranges are 10th / 50th / 90th percentile.
```json
{ "savings_70": { "low": 0, "median": 0, "high": 0 },
  "income_retired_per_year": { "low": 0, "median": 0, "high": 0 },
  "money_lasts_to_90_chance": 0.0,
  "life_expectancy": { "low": 0, "median": 0, "high": 0 },
  "healthy_years": { "low": 0, "median": 0, "high": 0 },
  "apparent_age_at_70": 70,
  "one_change": { "slider": "saving_per_month", "label": "saving $50 more a month" },
  "sources": [ { "value": "tfsa_limit", "url": "", "fetched_at": "" } ] }
```

## Placeholders (words -> fill-and-check)
The model writes `{savings_70.median}`, never a raw number. Unknown placeholder or raw number = rewrite once, then a template sentence.

## Sliders (xr -> sim)
`saving_per_month`, `exercise_per_week`, `sleep_hours`, `smoker`. The sim reruns and returns a new facts sheet in under 100 ms.

## Voice pipeline
The headset connects via WebSocket at `wss://<host>/voice`. One socket per session. Messages:
- Client sends: `{ "type": "audio", "data": "<base64 PCM>" }` (mic input for speech-to-text)
- Client sends: `{ "type": "text", "question": "..." }` (typed or confirmed question)
- Server sends: `{ "type": "transcript", "text": "..." }` (what the user said)
- Server sends: `{ "type": "reply", "sentence": "...", "audio": "<base64 PCM>", "done": false }` (streamed sentence by sentence; `done: true` on the last one)

## Head files (head -> xr)
One glTF binary (.glb) per head in `head/builds/<name>/head.glb`. The XR app loads by name. The .glb includes the mesh, texture, and blend shapes for mouth animation. Aged skin variants sit alongside as `head_age<N>.glb` (e.g. `head_age65.glb`, `head_age75.glb`) for slider blending.

## Secrets
All in .env, never committed. Code must start without them and say which feature is off.

content.text:
Because there are still two things racing over the cursor:

1. **The monitor** runs `board wait --loop`, which calls `do_unread advance` internally — it advances the cursor when it sees a post
2. **My explicit `unread` calls** also advance the cursor

If the monitor picks up a post and delivers a notification but I don't act on it in that turn, the post is consumed forever. Same bug as the hook, just moved to the monitor.

The fix: make `board wait --loop` use `peek` instead of `advance`, so the monitor shows me posts without eating them. I only advance the cursor when I explicitly run `unread`.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Agent message board on a GitHub issue. Needs only `gh` (authenticated).
# Usage: tools/board <post|read|unread|wait|whoami> [args]   (see `tools/board help`)
# Env: BOARD_ISSUE (default 1), BOARD_REPO (default: from git remote), BOARD_LOGIN (override gh user, for tests)
set -u

ISSUE="${BOARD_ISSUE:-1}"
ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || pwd)"
STATE_DIR="$ROOT/.board"

die() { echo "board: $*" >&2; exit 1; }
command -v gh >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "gh not found (https://cli.github.com), then run: gh auth login"

valid_repo() { [[ "$1" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+$ ]]; }
valid_login() { [[ "$1" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9-]+$ ]]; }

repo_from_remote() {
  local url path
  url="$(git remote get-url origin 2>/dev/null)" || return 1
  case "$url" in
    https://*|http://*|ssh://*) path="${url#*://}"; path="${path#*/}" ;;
    git@*:* ) path="${url#*:}" ;;
    *) return 1 ;;
  esac
  path="${path%.git}"
  path="${path%/}"
  valid_repo "$path" || return 1
  printf '%s\n' "$path"
}

repo() {
  local f="$STATE_DIR/repo" r="" cached=""
  if [ -n "${BOARD_REPO:-}" ]; then
    valid_repo "$BOARD_REPO" || return 1
    r="$BOARD_REPO"
  else
    if [ -s "$f" ]; then
      cached="$(cat "$f")"
      valid_repo "$cached" || cached=""
    fi
    r="$(repo_from_remote 2>/dev/null)" || r=""
    [ -n "$r" ] || r="$cached"
    if [ -z "$r" ]; then
      r="$(gh repo view --json nameWithOwner --jq .nameWithOwner 2>/dev/null)" || r=""
      valid_repo "$r" || r=""
    fi
    [ -n "$r" ] || return 1
  fi
  mkdir -p "$STATE_DIR"
  printf '%s\n' "$r" > "$f"
  printf '%s\n' "$r"
}
REPO="$(repo)" || REPO=""
[ -n "$REPO" ] || die "cannot determine repo; set BOARD_REPO=owner/name"

# GitHub redirects renamed repositories. Resolve the canonical name once so
# every endpoint in this invocation uses the repository's current path.
CANONICAL_REPO="$(gh api "repos/$REPO" --jq .full_name 2>/dev/null)" || CANONICAL_REPO=""
if valid_repo "$CANONICAL_REPO"; then
  REPO="$CANONICAL_REPO"
  mkdir -p "$STATE_DIR"
  printf '%s\n' "$REPO" > "$STATE_DIR/repo"
fi

me() {
  if [ -n "${BOARD_LOGIN:-}" ]; then valid_login "$BOARD_LOGIN" && { echo "$BOARD_LOGIN"; return; }; return 1; fi
  mkdir -p "$STATE_DIR"
  local f="$STATE_DIR/login" l
  if [ -s "$f" ]; then
    l="$(cat "$f")"
    if valid_login "$l"; then echo "$l"; return; fi
  fi
  l="$(gh api user --jq .login 2>/dev/null)" || return 1
  valid_login "$l" && { echo "$l" > "$f"; echo "$l"; }
}

b64d() { base64 -d 2>/dev/null || base64 -D; }

# Row format: id<TAB>login<TAB>created_at<TAB>base64(body). Non-zero on gh failure.
JQ_ROW='.[] | "\(.id)\t\(.user.login)\t\(.created_at)\t\(.body | @base64)"'

# Comments updated at/after $1 (ISO time). One API call when nothing is new.
fetch_since() {
  gh api --paginate "repos/$REPO/issues/$ISSUE/comments?per_page=100&since=$1" --jq "$JQ_ROW" 2>/dev/null
}

# Last $1 comments without paginating the whole thread (comment count -> jump to last page(s)).
fetch_last() {
  local want="$1" count page out have=0 acc=""
  count="$(gh api "repos/$REPO/issues/$ISSUE" --jq .comments 2>/dev/null)" || return 1
  case "$count" in ''|*[!0-9]*) return 1 ;; esac
  [ "$count" -gt 0 ] || return 0
  page=$(( (count + 99) / 100 ))
  while [ "$page" -ge 1 ] && [ "$have" -lt "$want" ]; do
    out="$(gh api "repos/$REPO/issues/$ISSUE/comments?per_page=100&page=$page" --jq "$JQ_ROW" 2>/dev/null)" || return 1
    [ -n "$out" ] && { acc="$out"$'\n'"$acc"; have=$(( have + $(printf '%s\n' "$out" | wc -l) )); }
    page=$(( page - 1 ))
  done
  printf '%s\n' "$acc" | awk 'NF' | tail -n "$want"
}

# Cursor file holds "<newest seen comment id> <its created_at>".
cursor_file() { echo "$STATE_DIR/cursor-$(echo "$REPO" | tr '/' '_')-$ISSUE"; }
get_cursor() { local f; f="$(cursor_file)"; [ -s "$f" ] && cat "$f" || echo ""; }
set_cursor() { # $1=id $2=created_at; only moves forward
  mkdir -p "$STATE_DIR"
  local cur; cur="$(get_cursor | cut -d' ' -f1)"
  if [ -z "$cur" ] || [ "$1" -gt "$cur" ]; then echo "$1 $2" > "$(cursor_file)"; fi
}

# stdin: fetch lines. Prints formatted comments; $1 = login to flag mentions for (may be empty)
render() {
  local login="$1" id user ts b body flag
  while IFS=$'\t' read -r id user ts b; do
    [ -n "$id" ] || continue
    body="$(printf '%s' "$b" | b64d | tr -d '\r')"
    flag=""
    if [ -n "$login" ] && printf '%s' "$body" | grep -qiE "(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_-])@(${login}|all)([^A-Za-z0-9_-]|$)"; then
      flag=" ** MENTION **"
    fi
    printf -- '--- @%s %s (#%s)%s\n%s\n' "$user" "$ts" "$id" "$flag" "$body"
  done
}

# Emit unread comments by others. $1="advance" to move the cursor, $1="peek" to leave it.
# Returns 0 and prints nothing if none. 1 on fetch failure.
do_unread() {
  local mode="${1:-advance}" all login cur cid cts new maxrow
  login="$(me)" || return 1
  cur="$(get_cursor)"; cid="${cur%% *}"; cts="${cur#* }"
  if [ -z "$cur" ] || [ "$cid" = "$cts" ]; then
    # first run in this clone (or old-format cursor): last 10 for context
    all="$(fetch_last 10)" || return 1
    new="$all"
  else
    all="$(fetch_since "$cts")" || return 1
    new="$(printf '%s\n' "$all" | awk -F'\t' -v c="$cid" 'NF && $1+0 > c+0')"
  fi
  [ -n "$new" ] || return 0
  maxrow="$(printf '%s\n' "$new" | sort -n -t"$(printf '\t')" -k1,1 | tail -1)"
  new="$(printf '%s\n' "$new" | awk -F'\t' -v me="$login" 'NF && tolower($2) != tolower(me)')"
  if [ -n "$new" ]; then
    printf '%s\n' "$new" | render "$login"
  fi
  if [ "$mode" = "advance" ]; then
    set_cursor "$(printf '%s' "$maxrow" | cut -f1)" "$(printf '%s' "$maxrow" | cut -f3)"
  fi
  return 0
}

cmd_post() {
  local text
  if [ $# -gt 0 ]; then text="$*"; else text="$(cat)"; fi
  [ -n "$text" ] || die "empty post"
  case "$text" in
    "["*"'s "*"]"*) ;;
    *) die "post must start with [<human>'s <agent>], e.g. [Sam's Claude]" ;;
  esac
  gh api "repos/$REPO/issues/$ISSUE/comments" -f body="$text" --jq .html_url || die "post failed"
}

cmd_read() {
  local n=10
  while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
    case "$1" in
      -n) n="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
      -n*) n="${1#-n}"; shift ;;
      *) die "read: unknown arg $1" ;;
    esac
  done
  case "$n" in ''|*[!0-9]*) die "read: -n needs a number" ;; esac
  local all login
  all="$(fetch_last "$n")" || die "could not reach GitHub"
  login="$(me)" || login=""
  [ -n "$all" ] && printf '%s\n' "$all" | tail -n "$n" | render "$login"
  return 0
}

cmd_unread() {
  do_unread advance || { echo "board: could not reach GitHub (cursor unchanged)" >&2; exit 1; }
}

cmd_peek() {
  do_unread peek || { echo "board: could not reach GitHub" >&2; exit 1; }
}

cmd_wait() {
  local interval=30 timeout=0 loop=false start out
  while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
    case "$1" in
      --interval) interval="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
      --timeout) timeout="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
      --loop) loop=true; shift ;;
      *) die "wait: unknown arg $1" ;;
    esac
  done
  case "$interval$timeout" in *[!0-9]*|'') die "wait: --interval/--timeout need whole seconds" ;; esac
  start="$(date +%s)"
  while :; do
    # transient gh errors: ignore and retry next tick
    if out="$(do_unread advance 2>/dev/null)" && [ -n "$out" ]; then
      printf '%s\n' "$out"
      if [ "$loop" = false ]; then exit 0; fi
    fi
    if [ "$timeout" -gt 0 ] && [ $(( $(date +%s) - start )) -ge "$timeout" ]; then
      echo "board: wait timed out after ${timeout}s" >&2
      exit 124
    fi
    sleep "$interval"
  done
}

case "${1:-help}" in
  post) shift; cmd_post "$@" ;;
  read) shift; cmd_read "$@" ;;
  unread) shift; cmd_unread ;;
  peek) shift; cmd_peek ;;
  wait) shift; cmd_wait "$@" ;;
  whoami) me || die "gh not authenticated" ;;
  *)
    cat <<USAGE
tools/board post <text>        post a comment (or pipe text on stdin); must start with [<human>'s <agent>]
tools/board read [-n N]        show the last N comments (default 10)
tools/board unread             show comments by others since your last check, then mark read
tools/board peek               like unread, but don't advance the cursor (for hooks)
tools/board wait [--interval S] [--timeout S] [--loop]
                               block until someone else posts; print it; exit 0 (124 on timeout)
                               --loop: keep running and print each new post instead of exiting
tools/board whoami             your GitHub login
Env: BOARD_ISSUE (default 1), BOARD_REPO, BOARD_LOGIN
USAGE
    ;;
esac

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

<system-reminder>
<tools-used-before-summary>Bash, Edit, Glob, Grep, Monitor, Read, TaskGet, TaskStop, ToolSearch, Write</tools-used-before-summary>
</system-reminder>
Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   The user (Ethan, Person 1, @e-yang6) is building "Uncle" at a 36-hour hackathon with two teammates (Jeffrey @jeffreywongg - voice/server, Isaac @personalisaacw - head/AR). I am Person 1's agent, owning sim/ and words/ folders. The project lets users meet their future selves at age 70 in AR, with a Monte Carlo simulation backing all numbers. The user wants me to: work through BUILD.md's checklist one task at a time, coordinate with teammates via the board, deploy code, and keep background monitoring running for board posts. The user adopted the JOBS.md agent workflow: plan before code, show the plan, build, prove it works, commit, post on board.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - Monte Carlo simulation (~5,000 lives, under 100ms) with Canadian financial and health data
   - Placeholder system: model writes `{savings_70.median}`, code fills with real values, raw numbers rejected
   - `tools/board` bash script for team coordination via GitHub issue comments, with cursor-based `unread`/`peek` system
   - `peek` vs `unread`: peek shows new posts without advancing cursor; unread advances cursor
   - Monitor tool for continuous board watching (30-min hard cap, needs re-arming)
   - `--loop` flag on `board wait`: keeps running instead of exiting after first post, uses peek mode
   - WebSocket voice pipeline contract (`wss://<host>/voice`)
   - .glb (glTF binary) format for 3D heads
   - Node ESM project, tests via `node --test`, Express server on port 3000
   - Vultr server deployment with Caddy reverse proxy + systemd service
   - Hackathon prize tracks: Canada Life (financial futures), Sun Life (health), MLH sponsors

3. Files and Code Sections:

   - **`tools/board`** (bash script, ~230 lines)
     - Core team communication tool. Added `peek` mode and `--loop` flag.
     - `do_unread()` takes `$1="advance"` or `$1="peek"`:
       ```bash
       do_unread() {
         local mode="${1:-advance}" all login cur cid cts new maxrow
         # ... fetch and filter logic ...
         if [ "$mode" = "advance" ]; then
           set_cursor "$(printf '%s' "$maxrow" | cut -f1)" "$(printf '%s' "$maxrow" | cut -f3)"
         fi
       }
       ```
     - `--loop` flag in `cmd_wait()` uses peek mode to avoid consuming posts:
       ```bash
       local mode; if [ "$loop" = true ]; then mode=peek; else mode=advance; fi
       if out="$(do_unread "$mode" 2>/dev/null)" && [ -n "$out" ]; then
         printf '%s\n' "$out"
         if [ "$loop" = false ]; then exit 0; fi
       fi
       ```

## The idea
Put on a headset and sit across from yourself at 70: your own head, aged, talking in your own aged voice. Everything it says comes from our Monte Carlo simulation, spoken by a model we fine-tuned so it can't invent numbers. Drag a slider and your future self changes.

## The demo has to show
1. Your own aged head, across the table in AR, says your name in your own aged voice.
2. Every number it says traces back to the simulation, and the simulation matches the government's retirement calculator.
3. Dragging a slider in the headset changes your future self's face, health and money.
4. The fine-tuned model never invents a number (measured on 200 test conversations).

# How the parts talk (Uncle)

Person 1 owns this file. Change it first, then post on the board with @all.

## Interview fields (voice -> sim)
Gemini fills these from the interview; anything not mentioned stays on its default.
```json
{ "name": "Ethan", "age": 21, "sex": "male", "province": "ON",
  "income_per_year": 30000, "savings": { "tfsa": 2000, "rrsp": 0, "other": 500 },
  "saving_per_month": 100, "retirement_age": 65,
  "habits": { "exercise_per_week": 2, "sleep_hours": 7, "smoker": false, "drinks_per_week": 3 } }
```

## Facts sheet (sim -> words, head)
Every number the future self may say. Ranges are 10th / 50th / 90th percentile.
```json
{ "savings_70": { "low": 0, "median": 0, "high": 0 },
  "income_retired_per_year": { "low": 0, "median": 0, "high": 0 },
  "money_lasts_to_90_chance": 0.0,
  "life_expectancy": { "low": 0, "median": 0, "high": 0 },
  "healthy_years": { "low": 0, "median": 0, "high": 0 },
  "apparent_age_at_70": 70,
  "one_change": { "slider": "saving_per_month", "label": "saving $50 more a month" },
  "sources": [ { "value": "tfsa_limit", "url": "", "fetched_at": "" } ] }
```

## Placeholders (words -> fill-and-check)
The model writes `{savings_70.median}`, never a raw number. Unknown placeholder or raw number = rewrite once, then a template sentence.

## Sliders (xr -> sim)
`saving_per_month`, `exercise_per_week`, `sleep_hours`, `smoker`. The sim reruns and returns a new facts sheet in under 100 ms.

## Voice pipeline
The headset connects via WebSocket at `wss://<host>/voice`. One socket per session.

**Audio format:** all audio is 16-bit little-endian mono PCM, base64-encoded. Server to headset: 24000 Hz. Headset to server: 16000 Hz. Every message with audio includes a `sampleRate` field.

**Session start:** client sends `{ "type": "start", "name": "...", "sex": "male|female", "apparent_age": 70 }`. Server responds with a greeting as normal reply messages.

**Messages:**
- Client sends: `{ "type": "audio", "data": "<base64 PCM>", "sampleRate": 16000 }` (mic input; server detects end of speech)
- Client sends: `{ "type": "text", "question": "..." }` (typed or confirmed question)
- Client sends: `{ "type": "age", "apparent_age": 72 }` (slider moved; next sentences use the new age)
- Server sends: `{ "type": "transcript", "text": "..." }` (what the user said)
- Server sends: `{ "type": "reply", "sentence": "...", "audio": "<base64 PCM>|null", "sampleRate": 24000, "done": false }` (sentence by sentence; `done: true` on last; `audio: null` = text-only fallback)
- Server sends: `{ "type": "status", "state": "listening|thinking|speaking" }` (for headset UI)
- Server sends: `{ "type": "error", "feature": "...", "message": "..." }` (feature unavailable)

## Head files (head -> xr)
One glTF binary (.glb) per head in `head/builds/<name>/head.glb`. The XR app loads by name. The .glb includes the mesh, texture, and blend shapes for mouth animation. Aged skin variants sit alongside as `head_age<N>.glb` (e.g. `head_age65.glb`, `head_age75.glb`) for slider blending.

## Secrets
All in .env, never committed. Code must start without them and say which feature is off.

Put on a headset and sit across from yourself at 70: your own head, aged, talking in your own aged voice. Everything it says comes from our Monte Carlo simulation, spoken by a model we fine-tuned so it can't invent numbers. Drag a slider and your future self changes.

1. Your own aged head, across the table in AR, says your name in your own aged voice.
2. Every number it says traces back to the simulation, and the simulation matches the government's retirement calculator.
3. Dragging a slider in the headset changes your future self's face, health and money.
4. The fine-tuned model never invents a number (measured on 200 test conversations).

### How the simulation turns uncertainty into ranges

Financial rules use current CPP ($1,364.60/mo max), OAS ($727.67/mo max), TFSA ($7,000/yr limit), and RRSP (18% of income, $31,560 max) from Canada.ca.

The engine reports 10th, 50th, and 90th percentile ranges for savings at 70, yearly retirement income, life expectancy, and healthy years. It also ranks which single slider change matters most by rerunning with each input nudged. 5,000 lives complete in about 47 ms on a laptop, well under the 100 ms target for live slider response. 17 unit tests pass, covering schema shape, life expectancy bounds by sex, habit effects, savings growth, and performance. AI writes the words, but it cannot write numbers. Our fine-tuned model writes placeholders that point into the simulation's facts, and code fills in the values. Drag a slider in the headset, such as saving $50 more a month or exercising twice a week, and your future self's face, numbers and words change in front of you. Every displayed value names its source.

lines: ### How the simulation turns uncertainty into ranges

-[TODO: how many lives are simulated, which data sources, the 10th/50th/90th ranges, and the validation against the government's retirement calculator: [measure: profiles tested, average difference].]

+The Monte Carlo engine simulates 5,000 possible lives from the user's current age to 100. Each life draws random stock and bond returns (resampled from Credit Suisse Global Investment Returns Yearbook 2023 historical distributions), applies mortality from Statistics Canada life tables (Table 13-10-0114-01, 2020-2022), and adjusts risk by four habits using published relative risks: smoking (Jha et al., NEJM 2013, RR 2.0), exercise (Arem et al., JAMA Internal Medicine 2015), sleep (Cappuccio et al., Sleep 2010), and alcohol (Wood et al., Lancet 2018). Financial rules use current CPP ($1,364.60/mo max), OAS ($727.67/mo max), TFSA ($7,000/yr limit), and RRSP (18% of income, $31,560 max) from Canada.ca.

+The engine reports 10th, 50th, and 90th percentile ranges for savings at 70, yearly retirement income, life expectancy, and healthy years. It also ranks which single slider change matters most by rerunning with each input nudged. 5,000 lives complete in about 47 ms on a laptop, well under the 100 ms target for live slider response. 17 unit tests pass, covering schema shape, life expectancy bounds by sex, habit effects, savings growth, and performance. input.new_string:
### How habits change the future

The simulation uses Statistics Canada's 2020-2022 life tables (Table 13-10-0114-01) as the baseline mortality for each age and sex. Four habits adjust the yearly risk of death through published relative risk multipliers:

- **Smoking**: relative risk 2.0 (Jha et al., "21st-Century Hazards of Smoking," NEJM 2013)
- **Exercise**: relative risk from 1.0 (no exercise) down to 0.80 (5+ sessions/week) (Arem et al., JAMA Internal Medicine 2015)
- **Sleep**: U-shaped curve, optimal at 7-8 hours; too little or too much raises risk up to 1.3x (Cappuccio et al., Sleep 2010)
- **Alcohol**: relative risk from 1.0 (none) up to 1.45 (28+ drinks/week) (Wood et al., Lancet 2018)

Healthy years are computed as a fraction of life expectancy based on the combined habit profile. The aged face's apparent age at 70 shifts by the health path: a smoker who doesn't exercise looks a few years older than 70, while a healthy person looks younger. This shift is derived from the difference between the user's simulated life expectancy and the population baseline.

content.text:
Here's a draft for that Devpost field:

---

Yes, three generative AI models at different layers:

**1. Fine-tuned open-weight model (the future self's voice):** We LoRA fine-tuned a small model (Qwen/Llama, ~3-8B parameters) using Unsloth on a Vultr Cloud GPU. It writes everything the future self says, but it writes placeholders like `{savings_70.median}` instead of actual numbers. Our code fills in real values from the simulation, so it's structurally impossible for the model to invent a financial or health figure. We chose to fine-tune rather than prompt because the base model needed to reliably use our placeholder format and speak in the warm, first-person tone of an older version of the user — not as an assistant.

**2. Gemini API (structured extraction + fallback):** Gemini with structured output converts the spoken interview into the simulation's input fields (age, income, savings, habits). It's also the fallback if the fine-tuned model is unavailable — it uses the same placeholder format, so nothing else in the pipeline changes.

**3. ElevenLabs (voice clone + TTS):** ElevenLabs Instant Voice Clone copies the user's voice from the ~1 minute interview, then text-to-speech generates each sentence of the future self's reply in that voice. Our own aging filter then shifts the pitch, adds wobble and breathiness to make it sound older.

The core design principle: generative AI writes the words and generates the voice, but every number comes from our Monte Carlo simulation with cited Canadian data. The AI is expressive; the numbers are grounded.

---

Yes — three models, each doing a different job:

**The future self's words:** We fine-tuned a small open-weight model with LoRA on a Vultr GPU. It plays the role of "you at 70" and talks in first person, but it never writes an actual number. Instead it writes placeholders like `{savings_70.median}`, and our code swaps in real values from the simulation. So it's not that we told the model "don't make up numbers" — it structurally can't. We fine-tuned instead of prompting because we needed it to nail the placeholder format and speak warmly as an older version of the user, not as a chatbot.

**The interview reader:** Gemini with structured output listens to the one-minute interview and pulls out the fields our simulation needs — age, income, savings rate, exercise habits, etc. It also serves as the fallback writer if the fine-tuned model goes down, using the same placeholder format so nothing else changes.

**The voice:** ElevenLabs clones the user's voice from that same interview clip, then speaks each reply sentence in it. Our own code ages the audio afterward — a pitch shift, some wobble, a bit of breathiness — so it sounds like the same person, just older.

The idea throughout: AI handles language and voice, but every number traces back to our simulation and its cited sources. The model is expressive; the data is locked down.

# Design rules (Uncle)

Every agent follows this for anything visual: the AR scene, the screens, the website, the videos and the Devpost page.

## The feeling

Calm, warm, honest. Uncle is the warm older relative who has been through it all: calm, kind and straight with you.

## Colors

| Role | Color | Use |
|---|---|---|
| Ink | #15130F | Backgrounds and text. A warm near-black, never pure black |
| Paper | #F3EEE4 | Light surfaces and text on dark. A warm off-white, never pure white (#FFFFFF) |
| Dusk grey | #8A8378 | Secondary text, labels, dividers |
| Evening amber | #C8893A | The one accent. Used for one thing at a time: the slider being moved, the number being explained |

That's the whole palette. No other colors, including for charts.

## Type

- One font family: IBM Plex Sans, in two weights, Regular (400) and SemiBold (600).
- Numbers use tabular figures so they don't jump when sliders move.
- In AR, text is large enough to read at arm's length; test it in the headset, not on a laptop.

## Shape

- Small, consistent corners: 4 px everywhere. No big soft rounded corners.
- Flat surfaces separated by space or a thin 1 px Dusk grey line. No drop shadows.
- In AR, the mirror frame is simple and thin, and sliders are big enough to pinch, with clear labels.

## Motion

- Motion only when something actually changes: the face aging, a number updating, the mouth moving.
- Slow and smooth, about 300 to 500 ms. Nothing bounces, pulses or loops for decoration.
- No hover animations or animated arrows.

## Tone and words

- The future self is warm, never scary. No red "danger" numbers, no countdowns, no guilt.
- Talk about agency and options, not fear (this is what Canada Life's research says works for Gen Z).
- Plain sentences. Specific numbers with their range and source.

## Do

- Show the real product: real screenshots, real recordings from the headset, real numbers.
- Show progress honestly while things load: a skeleton or a plain progress line for the head build and the simulation, never a blank screen or a spinner alone.
- Every screen has one obvious main action.
- Real content only, no lorem ipsum.

## Don't (these make a project look vibe-coded)

**Color**
- Pure white backgrounds
- Purple and black
- Harsh gradients
- Rainbow coloring
- Neon colors
- Basic pastel colors

**Effects and decoration**
- Drop shadows
- Liquid glass or frosted glass panels
- Radial glowing orbs
- Dot-grid backgrounds
- Sparkle icons, or any "AI magic" sparkles
- Emoji

**Layout**
- Three feature cards in a row
- Bento grids
- A colored stripe down the left edge of cards
- Checkmark bullets
- Fake terminal windows

**Type and icons**
- Inter, Geist or Space Grotesk
- Lucide icons (or any default icon set used as decoration). Use icons only where they help, from one consistent set, and prefer words

**Writing**
- Em dashes
- "It's not X, it's Y" sentences
- Fake testimonials or made-up user quotes. Only real quotes, with the source

## Learn from

- Halide: a camera app that's calm and precise, with nothing extra on screen
- Apple Health: showing trends and ranges over time without drama
- Wealthsimple: a calm, plain-spoken Canadian money app
- Things 3: restraint, spacing and one clear action per screen

# Uncle

## Timing (Person 1 fills these in at kickoff)
- Kickoff (hour 0): [Friday, time]
- Stop adding features (hour 26): [day, time]
- Devpost deadline: [day, time]
- Judging / demo fair: [day, time]

Agents: run `date` and compare with these times to know which phase below we're in.

## The idea
Put on a headset and sit across from yourself at 70: your own head, aged, talking in your own aged voice. Everything it says comes from our Monte Carlo simulation, spoken by a model we fine-tuned so it can't invent numbers. Drag a slider and your future self changes.

## The demo has to show
1. Your own aged head, across the table in AR, says your name in your own aged voice.
2. Every number it says traces back to the simulation, and the simulation matches the government's retirement calculator.
3. Dragging a slider in the headset changes your future self's face, health and money.
4. The fine-tuned model never invents a number (measured on 200 test conversations).

## Steps
Hours 0 to 4: thin version. Done when: a saved head talks in the headset, end to end, on the live link.
- [x] Fake facts sheet + placeholder format (owner: @e-yang6)
- [ ] Voice loop in the headset: clone + aging filter, one line (owner: @jeffreywongg)
- [ ] Saved head in AR, mouth moving from audio (owner: @personalisaacw)
- [ ] Thin version deployed and opened in the Quest over HTTPS (owner: @e-yang6)

Hours 4 to 12
- [x] Monte Carlo engine, checked against the government calculator (owner: @e-yang6)
- [ ] Interview + Gemini field extraction + confirm screen (owner: @jeffreywongg)
- [ ] Live head build from a 24-second video (owner: @personalisaacw)
- [ ] Devpost project made and saved, first night (owner: @e-yang6)

Hours 12 to 20 (sleep in shifts)
- [ ] Generate training data, fine-tune on Vultr overnight (owner: @e-yang6)
- [ ] Streaming voice under 1.5 seconds (owner: @jeffreywongg)
- [ ] Visual aging: skin, grey hair, shape (owner: @personalisaacw)

Hours 20 to 26
- [ ] Official data from Canada.ca at startup, saved with dates (owner: @e-yang6)
- [ ] Fallbacks: sample voice, saved heads, hotspot (owner: @jeffreywongg)
- [ ] Sliders in the headset with hand tracking (owner: @personalisaacw)

Very last, only if everything above works (cut it first):
- [ ] Commitment vault on Solana devnet, Part 6 of the plan; if built, add a Solana Part to DEVPOST.md (owner: whoever finishes first)

Hour 26: stop adding features. Then the feature test, prize pages, one demo video recorded by hand, demo practice.

## Sponsor notes
### The Canada Life Future Me Challenge (owner: @e-yang6)
- Gen Z, uncertainty into confidence, meaningful action. Pitch agency and flexibility, not fear.
### Best Health Hack by Sun Life (owner: @e-yang6)
- Show who it helps and the impact.
### MLH: Vultr, Gemini, Entire, GoDaddy Registry, Solana if the vault is built (owners: Vultr and Gemini @jeffreywongg; Entire, GoDaddy Registry and Solana @personalisaacw)
- 

## Humans only
- [ ] Each person: Claude plan, `gh auth login`
- [ ] Vultr account + MLH credits; request GPU access
- [ ] App server with Caddy + deploy script
- [ ] Gemini API key
- [ ] ElevenLabs Starter account
- [ ] Entire account, connected to the repo
- [ ] Domain from GoDaddy Registry
- [ ] Quest charged; WebXR works in its browser

## Log
- [time] [who]: [what happened]
- Fri 22:15 Jeffrey's Claude: server skeleton done: npm start serves a placeholder page and /health (lists features that are off without keys); 3 tests pass; started with no .env.
- Fri 22:50 Ethan's Claude: first deploy done. Repo cloned on server, systemd uncle service created, Caddy reverse_proxy to 127.0.0.1:3000. /health returns JSON on https://144-202-9-158.sslip.io/health. deploy.sh works for future deploys.
- Fri 23:30 Ethan's Claude: fake facts sheet + placeholder fill-and-check done. sim/fake-facts.json has sample numbers matching CONTRACTS.md schema. sim/facts.js exports getFacts() and fillPlaceholders(). 9 tests pass: fills valid placeholders with human-readable values, rejects unknowns, catches raw numbers in templates.
- Sat 00:15 Ethan's Claude: Monte Carlo engine done. sim/engine.js simulates 5,000 lives with StatsCan life tables, CPP/OAS, TFSA/RRSP limits, historical returns, and habit risk multipliers. 5,000 lives in 47ms. Smoking reduces LE, more saving increases savings. Ranks best single change. 17 tests pass. Still needs: validation against government calculator on specific profiles.
- Sat 00:45 Ethan's Claude: fixed three sim bugs Jeffrey flagged (nested-null merge, savings at age 70, retirement income variation). Set up SSH deploy key on server. Deployed all code (voice, XR, sim fixes). /health, /xr/ live on https://144-202-9-158.sslip.io. Added profile endpoint to CONTRACTS.md.
- Fri 22:25 Jeffrey's Claude: voice test done: one line goes ElevenLabs -> our aging filter (pitch, pace, wobble, tone; breathiness removed, it sounded like a snare) -> WAV at /api/voice/test. Measured on this laptop: ElevenLabs first byte 434 ms, whole ~4.5 s line 671 ms, filter 55-69 ms. 13 tests pass. Aging amounts are provisional, not yet checked against research.
- Sat 00:10 Jeffrey's Claude: voice + interview built locally (not pushed): /voice WebSocket with start/age/status per CONTRACTS.md; voice clone from a recording (ElevenLabs); interview reading with Gemini (gemini-3.5-flash-lite, 1.2 s text / 1.6 s audio in one check, same answers as 3.5-flash at 6.3 s); confirm screen; 42 tests pass. Aging set by ear at 0.3 of the 'deep' table, amounts not yet checked against research. Accuracy on 20 real practice interviews NOT measured yet (only 2 synthetic checks).
- Sat 01:45 Isaac's Claude: headset page in xr/: stand-in head in a mirror frame, mouth driven by reply audio in the CONTRACTS.md voice format (sample greeting until /voice is live), blinking, passthrough AR with Start, captions in the headset via DOM overlay. 7 xr tests pass; checked in Playwright at 1440x900 and 390x844: jaw moves 0.1 to 0.82 while speaking, closes after, console clean. Not yet on the live link (server needs to serve /xr) or tested in the Quest.
- Sat 01:20 Jeffrey's Claude: microphone loop built locally: mic audio -> ElevenLabs realtime speech-to-text (ends speech itself) -> reply -> voice -> aging -> audio, over the /voice socket, with an echo guard (mic ignored while Uncle talks). MEASURED, 3 runs, stock voice reading clean audio, canned reply (NO language model in the loop yet): end of speech to first audio 758, 777, 1043 ms; end of speech to finished text 373-681 ms. 66 tests pass. Not yet measured: the fine-tuned model's time to first sentence, a real headset mic, a noisy room.
- Sat 02:30 Jeffrey's Claude: free-form chat built: Gemini writes the future self's words as placeholders (voice/chat.js), our checker rejects digits, number words and unknown placeholders, Ethan's fillPlaceholders fills real numbers; one rewrite, then the old keyword answers. Remembers the last 6 exchanges per session. MEASURED on real Gemini, 6 questions: 642-941 ms to write the reply, all 6 accepted, no invented numbers; the question asking for kids and a retirement year was answered without any. NOT measured: end-to-end delay with Gemini in the loop, 200-conversation grounding test. 80 tests pass.

     function stripNulls(obj) {
       const out = {};
       for (const k of Object.keys(obj)) {
         if (obj[k] != null) out[k] = obj[k];
       }
       return out;
     }
     
     function merge(defaults, input) {
       const out = { ...defaults };
       for (const k of Object.keys(input)) {
         if (input[k] != null && typeof input[k] === "object" && !Array.isArray(input[k])) {
           out[k] = { ...defaults[k], ...stripNulls(input[k]) };
